text: A field is a nontrivial commutative ring in which every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse. Inversion at zero is defined as zero, so division by zero is also zero, while cancellation still requires a nonzero denominator. Positive characteristic is allowed; the included rational-number conversion need not be an embedding. Compared with [Stacks 09FD](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09FD) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Field/Defs.lean#L180).

A division ring has the usual ring laws, is nontrivial, and gives every nonzero element an inverse; multiplication need not commute. Division a/b means a multiplied on the right by b’s inverse, so order matters. Zero’s inverse and division by zero are defined as zero, without extending nonzero cancellation to zero. Compared with [Judson §16.1](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Field/Defs.lean#L116).

This is an additive monoid with a designated element one and the canonical natural-number map: zero maps to zero, and each successor adds one. Addition is associative with identity zero but need not commute. One need not differ from zero, and the natural-number map need not be injective. Compared with [Aspnes §4.6](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Nat/Cast/Defs.lean#L65).

This is an additive group with a designated one and compatible natural-number and integer maps. Nonnegative integers use repeated addition of one; negative integers use additive inverses. Addition need not commute, and one need not be nonzero. These maps are therefore canonical but need not be injective. Compared with [Aspnes §4.6](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Int/Cast/Defs.lean#L41).

This adds commutative addition to an additive monoid with a designated one and its natural-number map. Natural numbers still mean repeated addition of one. Multiplication and additive inverses are not part of the structure, and one may equal zero; no characteristic-zero or injectivity assertion is hidden in the name. Compared with [Aspnes §§4.1.1,4.6](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Nat/Cast/Defs.lean#L73).

Characteristic zero here means that distinct natural numbers remain distinct after conversion by repeated addition of one. This agrees with the usual condition for rings. For arbitrary additive monoids it is stronger than saying no positive integer maps to zero: different positive coefficients could coincide without either becoming zero. Compared with [Judson §16.2](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/CharZero/Defs.lean#L44).

A finite set is represented by a finite collection with no repeated elements, where rearranging the underlying list makes no difference. Thus membership has no order or multiplicity. The surrounding type may be infinite, and the empty finite set is allowed; the definition does not require a supplied equality-decision procedure. Compared with [Aspnes §§3.1,9.4.1](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Finset/Defs.lean#L75).

A finite-type structure supplies a finite set containing every element of the type. Because that set has no duplicates, it is an exhaustive enumeration without repeated entries. This carries enumeration data, unlike the bare assertion of finiteness. Empty types are allowed, with the empty set as their enumeration. Compared with [Aspnes §3.5.5.4](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Fintype/Defs.lean#L57).

A type is finite when it is in bijection with the numbers 0,…,n−1 for some natural number n. This is an existence statement, not a chosen enumeration or algorithm. The case n=0 includes empty types, and the definition also applies to propositions, whose proofs cannot give distinct elements. Compared with [Aspnes §3.5.5.4](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Finite/Defs.lean#L101).

Nontrivial means that there exist two distinct elements. It therefore excludes both empty types and one-element types; it is stronger than mere nonemptiness. No arithmetic or other structure is assumed. For rings this recovers the familiar requirement that zero and one differ, while the definition itself applies to any type. Compared with [Aspnes §§3.1,3.5.5.4](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Nontrivial/Defs.lean#L28).

A subgroup is a subset of a group containing the identity and closed under multiplication and inverses. The operations are inherited from the ambient group, so associativity follows automatically. The identity-only subgroup and the whole group are included, but the empty subset is excluded; neither finiteness nor commutativity is required. Compared with [Judson §3.3.1](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Defs.lean#L296).

A submodule contains zero and is closed under addition and every scalar multiplication from the given semiring. This includes ordinary subspaces and modules, but also semimodules without additive inverses. Its operations are inherited from the ambient structure; closure under negation follows in the ring case, rather than being separately required here. Compared with [Schweigert Def.1.1.21](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Submodule/Defs.lean#L39).

A matrix is an array of entries indexed by a row type and a column type: its value at row i and column j is an entry. Neither index type is required to be finite, and entries need no arithmetic structure. Matrix operations and finite-sum multiplication impose their additional assumptions separately. Compared with [Aspnes §9.1.2](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Defs.lean#L56).

An equivalence consists of a forward map and a backward map whose two composites are identities. It therefore represents a bijection with its inverse, not merely an injective map or an equivalence relation on one set. No algebraic structure is preserved unless additional requirements are supplied by a more specialized notion. Compared with [Aspnes §§3.5.4–3.5.5](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Defs.lean#L65).

This is a commutative ring with a multiplicative identity, except that multiplication is not required to be associative. Addition remains an abelian group, and both distributive laws hold. The qualifier permits associative examples too; it does not assert failure of associativity. The zero ring is allowed, since nontriviality is not required. Compared with [Judson §16.1](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Defs.lean#L399).

A monoid homomorphism is a function preserving multiplication and the designated one. The definition also permits structures with just these operations, before associativity or identity laws are assumed. For actual monoids it is the usual unital homomorphism; for groups inverse preservation follows, and injectivity or surjectivity is never required. Compared with [Judson §11.1](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Hom/Defs.lean#L366).

A scalar tower expresses compatibility of three scalar operations: first letting x act on y and then on z agrees with letting y act on z and then x act on the result. Only this associativity equation is imposed. Modules, ring inclusions and faithful actions are useful examples, not additional assumptions. Compared with [Schweigert Lem.1.1.23](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Action/Defs.lean#L208).

This structure supplies a distinguished one and an inverse operation satisfying only that the inverse of one is one. It does not include multiplication, so it cannot by itself assert cancellation or that other elements have multiplicative inverses. It isolates the familiar identity-inverse law for reuse in stronger structures. Compared with [Judson §3.2](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/DivInvMonoid.lean#L288).

This structure supplies zero and a negation operation with the equation −0=0. Addition, additive cancellation and double-negation laws are not included. Thus it records one familiar property of additive inverses without claiming that negation already comes from a group; stronger algebraic structures provide the remaining laws separately. Compared with [Judson §3.2](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/DivInvMonoid.lean#L280).

This specifies a multiplication with a two-sided identity one: multiplying by one on either side leaves an element unchanged. Associativity, commutativity and inverses are not required, so the structure need not be a monoid. The two separate identity laws matter because multiplication is otherwise an arbitrary binary operation. Compared with [Judson §3.2](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Monoid.lean#L74).

This specifies an addition with zero as a two-sided identity: 0+a=a and a+0=a. It does not assume associativity, commutativity or additive inverses, so the structure need not be an additive monoid. Both identity equations are required independently, and a one-element structure is allowed. Compared with [Judson §3.2](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Monoid.lean#L65).

This bundles a binary multiplication and a distinguished element named one, with no equations connecting them. In particular, one is not yet required to act as an identity, and multiplication need not be associative. It provides the operations used by later structures; their identity and associativity assumptions are added separately. Compared with [Judson §3.2](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Monoid.lean#L37).

This bundles a binary addition and a distinguished element named zero, without requiring zero to be an additive identity. Associativity, commutativity and inverse laws are also absent. It is the underlying operation data on which stronger additive structures are built, so those familiar laws require additional hypotheses. Compared with [Judson §3.2](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Monoid.lean#L32).

This stores a natural-number power operation, taking an exponent and a base to an output. By itself it imposes no multiplication, identity or power laws. When incorporated into a monoid, additional laws require exponent zero to give one and successor exponents to multiply once more; those laws belong to the stronger structure. Compared with [Judson §3.2](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Monoid.lean#L365).

A set of elements of a fixed type is represented by its membership predicate. Two sets are equal when they contain exactly the same elements; listing order and multiplicity have no role. Sets may be empty or infinite, and the definition requires neither a finite enumeration nor an algorithm deciding membership. Compared with [Aspnes §§3.1,3.3](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Defs.lean#L48).

A right comodule has a linear coaction M → M⊗C, coassociative and counital, as in [Milne §4.a, equation (24)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The explicit associator aligns the tensor parentheses; the counit returns m⊗1 before the canonical identification M⊗R ≅ M. The same equations make sense over commutative semirings, without finite-dimensionality or flatness. Checks pass: [coassoc_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L90), [lTensor_counit_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L98), [instSelf_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L161).
Pointwise coassociativity retains the tensor associator.
Counit gives m tensor 1 before the right unitor.
The regular comodule realizes the definition by comultiplication.

The coalgebra C becomes its regular right comodule by taking the coaction to be its comultiplication Δ. Its two required laws are precisely coalgebra coassociativity and the right counit identity. This agrees with the comodule (C, Δ) in [Milne §9.d](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=185); neither a multiplication on C nor an antipode is required. Checks pass: [instSelf_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L161), [coassoc_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L90).
The stored regular coaction is exactly comultiplication.
Regular specialization satisfies the actual comodule associativity equation.

A comodule morphism is a linear map f satisfying (f⊗id)ρ_M = ρ_N f: it preserves the coaction over the same fixed coalgebra. This is the intertwining notion behind [Milne §9.d](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=185). The added field is a proof of this equality, so morphisms retain no extra mathematical data beyond their underlying linear maps. Checks pass: [map_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L235), [toLinearMap_injective](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L216).
The intertwining equality evaluates on each vector.
Forgetting the compatibility proof is injective.

A comodule morphism acts on vectors through its underlying linear map. Equality of these functions determines the linear map and hence the comodule morphism, because compatibility is a property, not additional data. Thus this function interpretation faithfully realizes the morphisms of [Milne §9.d](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=185); it does not assert that every function is a morphism. Checks pass: [coe_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L207), [ext](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L223).
Function coercion agrees with the underlying linear map.
Pointwise equality determines the comodule morphism.

Composition of comodule morphisms is ordinary composition of their linear maps: comp(g,f) sends m to g(f(m)). Tensor-product functoriality and the two intertwining equations prove that this composite again respects the coaction. This supplies the expected composition in [Milne §9.d](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=185), over the fixed coalgebra and without an injectivity assumption. Checks pass: [comp_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L270), [comp_assoc](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L286).
Underlying composite is g after f.
Composition is associative as comodule morphisms.

The identity linear map respects every coaction, since tensoring identity maps acts identically on the tensor product. It therefore supplies the identity comodule morphism of [Milne §9.d](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=185). The construction retains the given comodule structure, and the native identity laws check both orders of composition, without assuming that the comodule is finite. Checks pass: [id_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L276), [comp_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L281).
Identity on the target is a left identity.
Identity on the source is a right identity.

Given a linear functional φ on C, this endomorphism contracts the C-factor of the coaction: Σ mᵢ⊗cᵢ becomes Σ φ(cᵢ)mᵢ. This is the dual-coalgebra action associated with [Milne §9.d](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=185). Tensor contraction makes the result independent of the displayed tensor expression; no choice of basis or assertion that functionals separate vectors is needed. Checks pass: [coactComponent_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L129), [tensorComponent_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basic.lean#L61).
Definition is contraction after coaction.
Contraction on a pure tensor is the expected scalar multiple.

A comodule structure on fixed scalar, coalgebra and module structures is determined by its coaction map. Coassociativity and counitality, the equations in [Milne §4.a, equation (24)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), are properties of that map rather than additional choices. The displayed coact = coact uses two different implicit structures, rho and sigma. It identifies those structures, not different carrier modules. Checks pass: [instSelf_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L161), [of_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cat.lean#L73).
The regular structure has the specified coaction.
Bundling preserves the supplied coaction exactly.

Applying the counit to the coalgebra factor of ρ(m) gives m⊗1 in M⊗R. This is exactly the counitality equation of [Milne §4.a, equation (24)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95) before applying the canonical right tensor identification M⊗R ≅ M. The explicit tensor target prevents interpreting the displayed equality as an untyped equality with m itself. Checks pass: [tensorComponent_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basic.lean#L56).
Contraction includes the right tensor unitor.

Coassociativity makes successive contractions act by convolution: Tφ(Tψ(m)) = T_(φ*ψ)(m), where (φ*ψ)(c) = Σ φ(c₁)ψ(c₂). This matches the dual multiplication in [Milne §9.d](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=185). The order is φ then ψ on the coproduct factors, even though ψ acts first on m; cocommutativity is not assumed. Checks pass: [coact_comp_tensorComponent](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L106), [tensorComponent_comp_tensorComponent](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basic.lean#L98), [coassoc_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L90).
Coaction commutes with contraction on the other factor.
Two contractions combine after reassociation.
Coassociativity supplies the coproduct appearing in convolution.

For each m, coacting twice on the module factor equals coacting once and comultiplying the coalgebra factor. The associator sends (M⊗C)⊗C to M⊗(C⊗C), making the equality correctly typed. This is the pointwise form of [Milne §4.a, equation (24)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95); it does not interchange the two coalgebra factors or require cocommutativity. Checks pass: [coact_coassoc](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L82), [coactComponent_coactComponent](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L134).
The full linear-map coassociativity equation specializes to vectors.
Contraction reads the same equation as ordered convolution.

This is the vectorwise intertwining identity: coacting after f equals applying f on the module factor after coacting. The coalgebra factor stays unchanged, so both sides lie in N⊗C. It directly expresses the comodule morphisms of [Milne §9.d](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=185), with no assumption that f is injective, surjective or invertible. Checks pass: [map_coact_eq](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L228), [comp_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L270).
The vector identity comes from equality of linear maps.
Composition retains the underlying composite of intertwiners.

An object bundles a semimodule together with its right coaction over a fixed coalgebra, the category considered in [Milne §9.d](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=185). Scalar coefficients here may form a commutative semiring, so additive inverses are not required. Finite-dimensionality is not part of this object, and this definition alone makes no claim that the category is abelian. Checks pass: [of_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cat.lean#L73), [forget₂_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cat.lean#L307).
Bundling an existing comodule preserves its coaction.
Forgetting returns the original semimodule.
